text:
Allison Grant: heads up for status page transparency upgrades — we need better signal-to-component mapping. proposal: add `status_component` label to a small set of core metrics so dashboards can answer “what’s impacted?” without hand-waving. anyone objecting / got caveats re cardinality?

Aisha Bello: +1. right now we can say “5xx up” but support keeps asking “is it streaming only?” we need breakdown by component (Streaming vs API Gateway vs Embeddings etc). if we can tag errors/latency with `status_component` we can build the exact dashboard panels we want.

Christine Wong: what’s the source of truth for `status_component`? the taxonomy doc lists components but services don’t map 1:1. ex: router service touches both chat + embeddings sometimes.

Miles Thornton: for incident-bot, we’re already adding an internal “customer impact classifier” helper. would be great if metrics agree with what bot suggests. but i’m wary of trying to infer component at query-time.

Dylan Brooks: cardinality is the big risk. if we add `status_component` + `route` + `model` + `region` on histograms, we’ll nuke prom/grafana.

Allison Grant: yep. constraint proposal:
- `status_component` is an enum of *public* status page components only (no internal service names)
- required labels for impacted metrics: `status_component`, `region` (existing), maybe `deployment_mode` (hosted/dedicated/private) where applicable
- explicitly do NOT add `customer_id`, `model_id`, or raw `path`
- for routes: only coarse `route_group` (chat|embeddings|rerank|console) if needed

Sara Al-Masri: +1 to “public components only”. we can keep `status_component` small: `api_gateway`, `streaming`, `embeddings`, `rerank`, `console`, `hosted_serving`, `dedicated_control_plane`, `private_control_plane`, `capacity_routing`?

Mina Haddad: naming: please keep it aligned with status page names. “capacity_routing” is that the customer-friendly “Capacity & Routing” from the taxonomy thread? we should avoid “scheduler”.

Ethan Park: implementation detail: i can add this label at emission time from control plane services for the request/response metrics. but for “hosted_serving” (runtime) we need runtime team to emit it too. otherwise dashboards are half-blind.

Nora Ahmed: from a UX perspective, having dashboards mirror the status components is super helpful. support + PM can literally say “this graph corresponds to status component X”.

Dylan Brooks: which metrics exactly are we tagging? please not every histogram.

Allison Grant: scoping to “status-page relevant metrics” only:
1) request error counters (5xx, 429, timeouts) for hosted API
2) streaming disconnect / keepalive timeout counter
3) latency SLO-ish histograms but only for `status_component` + `region` (no additional dims)
4) console API error rate
5) dedicated/private control plane API availability

Aisha Bello: also need a panel for “likely customer impact classification” so oncall can choose degraded vs partial outage. doesn’t have to be perfect, but should point to which component is burning.

Miles Thornton: +1. incident-bot could link that dashboard directly in the prompts.

Christine Wong: question: what about incidents that are model-family specific? status page taxonomy mentions “model-family incidents” (e.g. llama-3 family). do we need label for that too?

Allison Grant: not as a metric label (too high cardinality + changes often). we can do a separate log-based indicator for “model family” in the incident timeline, but the primary breakdown for comms is component+region.

Dylan Brooks: ok. for prom label cardinality, can we cap `status_component` values in code? like reject unknown values so someone can’t start emitting `status_component=request-123` by accident.

Sara Al-Masri: we can enforce via shared constants library + unit test in instrumentation wrapper.

Ethan Park: i can add schema validation for structured incident annotations too (we already have a PR draft for emitting annotations from control plane). similar approach.

Mina Haddad: also watch out for region naming. status page uses `us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-west`. some metrics use `us-east-1` etc. we need normalization or the dashboards will mislead.

Allison Grant: good call — we should normalize to status-page region slugs at ingestion or via recording rules.

Aisha Bello: dashboard asks (from support):
- top components by error budget burn last 1h/24h
- “streaming-only errors” toggle
- region heatmap
- link to current incident + latest status page update timestamp (so we can see when comms is stale)

Miles Thornton: last item is clutch. if we can surface “time since last status update” in the same dashboard, it’ll prevent the ‘we’re investigating’ dead-air problem.

Grafana Bot: Allison Grant created dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/impact-status/status-page-impact (access: eng-platform)

Allison Grant: draft dashboard is WIP but shows how `status_component` would be used. note: panels are currently mocked with `service` label; will swap once we have `status_component`.

Dylan Brooks: :eyes: can you annotate which panels are “must-have” for v1 vs nice-to-have? we can land the label changes incrementally.

Allison Grant: v1 must-have panels:
- Errors by `status_component` + region (stacked)
- Streaming disconnects by region
- p95 latency by `status_component` + region (coarse)
- Console 5xx by region
- Dedicated/private control plane availability (global + by region if exists)

Christine Wong: if we don’t have runtime metrics tagged, “hosted_serving” will look green when streaming is red (or vice versa). can we explicitly split gateway vs runtime vs streaming?

Ethan Park: we can. gateway metrics = `api_gateway`, runtime inference metrics = `hosted_serving`, streaming protocol metrics = `streaming`. that matches the kinds of customer complaints we’ve had.

Mina Haddad: and for capacity constraints / routing (429s due to capacity), those should map to “Capacity & Routing” component, not “API Gateway” if the gateway is healthy.

Aisha Bello: yes please. status page accuracy depends on not lumping 429s w/ “gateway down”.

Miles Thornton: for incident-bot, we can also special-case: if 429 spike + capacity signals, suggest selecting “Capacity & Routing” and add customer guidance (backoff, fallback models, region pinning).

Sara Al-Masri: action item: can someone define mapping rules for 429s? e.g. `error_type=rate_limited` vs `capacity_exhausted`.

Ethan Park: i can add `throttle_reason` as a *bounded enum* label to the 429 counter only (NOT to latency histograms). values: `user_quota`, `org_quota`, `capacity`, `abuse_protection`, `unknown`. then the dashboard can attribute to component.

Dylan Brooks: that’s acceptable if it stays bounded + only on that one counter.

Allison Grant: ok, plan:
- (Ethan) add `status_component` + normalized `region` to hosted gateway + control plane metrics, plus bounded `throttle_reason` on 429 counter
- (Allison) update recording rules + dashboard to use new labels
- (Aisha) define SLO burn -> “impact language” thresholds per component for comms (degraded vs partial outage)
- (Miles/Sara) link dashboard + component suggestions into incident-bot prompts

Christine Wong: timeline? we need this before we roll out the new status components.

Allison Grant: aiming end of week for label emission in gateway/control plane, next week for dashboards. runtime tags might lag (separate thread w/ eng-runtime) but we can still get immediate win for streaming/gateway/console.

Aisha Bello: works. once dashboards are live, i’ll run through 2-3 past incidents to confirm the “what’s impacted” view matches what we would’ve posted.

Dylan Brooks: please add a note in the PR about label cardinality + allowed values. reviewers will ask.

Ethan Park: will do. i’ll include a const list and guardrail in the instrumentation wrapper.

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup: and please ping me on the region normalization bit. i’ve got a mapping table from routing.

Allison Grant: will ping. thanks all — this should meaningfully reduce the “is it streaming-only?” confusion.

Nora Ahmed: (reaction: :+1:) if you want, i can sanity-check the component names as they show up in grafana so they match what customers see.

Allison Grant: yes please. i’ll DM you when the dashboard labels are swapped.
